g.text: Chat ends. Next chat will be ArthurSkana.
You've been... I'm not the easiest man to get to know. You've put up with me dodging.
To be fair, I've been doing the same thing to you about what made me, me. Duviri, and all...
Talking about the dark parts of our past isn't easy or fun for anybody.
Yeah. About time you man up, cowboy.
Well, the point is, you've been waiting around trying to get the whole story out of me -
And immediately? I've changed my mind.
how I got here, how I got like this,
the rest of the story about this sword,
and all the rest of this ugly mess...
Pour yourself a cup of tea.
Actually, a beer would be best.
I'll try to make this brief. Sol knows I don't want to dwell on this shit any more than I need to.
Take the time you need. I'm here.
I told you why I left the Britannic Army. I never told you why I joined.
When I was a lad, there was a childhood friend a few years above Eleanor and I in school. Lived a few doors up the street.
This skana of mine that you've asked after.
The bandana I keep on my blade?
Eleanor told me her half of the Christopher story already.
Name was Christopher. He was always sticking up for the kids in the neighborhood who needed it.
I told you how I got it. Entrati running me through with it. Not long after he turned me into this...
I got it when Entrati ran me through with it. Not long after he turned me into this...
Christopher got it for me... as a gift for joining the Crimson Watch.
There was... an old friend of mine, way back in the day.
He was bigger, tougher - smarter. One of those blokes you'd want to push in front of a lorry if he wasn't so damned NICE all the time.
He was planning on giving it to me the night I got there.
I... can't thank you enough for being there for her. For finally being someone who might get her past what she lost on that terrible day.
She... lost a lot more than me, that day.
In short? I bloody wanted to BE him, growing up. Followed in his footsteps any way I could.
But I dodged when you asked me about the bandana.
But it's not the blade that's important to me. It's the bandana.
You. You're just YOU. Inside. Where it counts.
It was waiting for me... instead of him.
Christopher? Eleanor told me some of it.
It was meant to be a gift. He never got to deliver it to me.
She makes it sound like you both lost someone special.
But it sounds like you both lost someone that meant a lot to you.
I was lucky enough to call my idol my best friend.
I... will never adjust to that.
Thanks. I need to remember that.
What happened to him isn't your fault, Arthur.
War takes the best of us away.
He was a dear friend and I looked up to him like a big brother. I idolized him.
So when he went off and joined His Majesty's Service, as soon as he was of age? I was biting at the bit, waiting until I was old enough to do the same.
Well. That's how I got the blade.
I know. But it is my duty to carry on.
Christopher represented everything I wanted to be in this world - noble, heroic, self-sacrificing.
Never mind the fact that he...
Thank you for being there for her. For helping her heal.
He was bigger, tougher - smarter. One of those blokes you'd want to push in front of a lorry if he wasn't so damned NICE all the time.
Look, Drifter... This part isn't my story to tell. It's Eleanor's. But I'll say this much. When Christopher went off to war?
But sometimes, an old ghost is a welcome one.
You've helped me heal a lot of that old pain, by being here for me.
So when he went off and joined His Majesty's Service, as soon as he was of age? I was biting at the bit, waiting until I was old enough to do the same.
I wasn't the only one upset to see him go.
They remind us of why we're still here. Who we were before.
Imagine poor Eleanor, having to watch her fiancé and her twin brother go off to war.
He must have really meant a lot to you.
She never trusted authority. But after what happened to the two of us? She never would again.
Christopher had pulled some strings. Lined it up so that I'd be in the same regiment as him. 3rd Battalion, Crimson Watch.
And who we're still fighting for.
I can't say I blame her.
But one week before I got out there... there was an incident. Roadside bomb.
I... never really had anyone to fight for. Not until recently. One reason they call me 'Drifter.'
I've run out of imaginary beers to drink. I kind of need a real one, now.
And like so many good men and women? Like so many good soldiers?
I can't tell which one of us has had it worse. Both. Neither.
You haven't had it much better than me, have you, though?
He became just another number on somebody's sheet.
Creations of war, just in different ways. We've both lost a lot in our lives.
But I was still a naive fool. And I, like an idiot, was all too eager to pick up the mantle he left behind...
No one wins in war. No one.
I... yeah. But. That was... heavy. Drinks? You and me? Then we go find a quiet place to talk in person?
We've both lost things, yes. But look at how much we've found. Friends. Family. Each other.
You lost... one guy? All this was about *one* guy? I was expecting something way more dramatic.
Look at what we've been able to do here.
Love, nothing would make me happier right now.
You're right. Enough of this moody shit for one day.
